key_observations: 40m macro with full 4-band stack (700/1800/2600/3500 MHz) provides coverage depth via 700 MHz and 5G peak throughput via 3500 MHz.
6 5G cells vs 4 4G cells — 5G-dominant with meaningful 4G fallback layer for legacy devices.
Capacity score 25.6 is tied-highest in the neighborhood alongside USID_29 and USID_37 — well-provisioned for its edge-limited footprint.
20m micro with only 2 bands (2600/3500 MHz — no 700 or 1800 MHz) — high-band-only capacity fill node; no low-band coverage layer limits propagation range.
8 5G cells vs 2 4G cells is the highest 5G-to-4G ratio in the neighborhood; strongly supports the capacity-oriented operational role.
Capacity score 23.4 is strong despite micro form factor; however, lack of 700 MHz band reduces resilience in building-penetration or marginal coverage scenarios.
Identical hardware profile to USID_00 (40m macro, 4 bands, 4×4G + 6×5G) — near-perfect configuration substitute for the target site.
Full 700 MHz low-band ensures coverage continuity even at the outer edge of the handover zone.
Capacity score 25.6 matches USID_00 exactly — no capacity downgrade for handed-over users.
35m macro with only 2 bands (1800/2600 MHz — no 700 MHz low-band, no 3500 MHz 5G NR band) — legacy mid-band site with minimal 5G investment.
8 4G cells vs 2 5G cells makes this the most 4G-heavy site; capacity score 15.6 is ~39% below the neighborhood average of ~24.
Users handed over from USID_00 to USID_41 will likely experience 4G fallback given only 2 5G cells and no 3500 MHz band — a notable service step-down from USID_00's 5G-dominant profile.
Identical hardware profile to USID_00 and USID_29 (40m macro, 4 bands, 4×4G + 6×5G) — third macro-5G site in the neighborhood providing configuration parity.
Full band diversity including 700 MHz ensures reliable service throughout the handover zone.
Capacity score 25.6 and 5G-dominant profile mean 5G users from USID_00 find equivalent 5G service with no throughput regression.
48m tall_macro with full 4-band stack (700/1800/2600/3500 MHz) — tallest site in the group, optimized for wide-area coverage propagation.
6 4G cells vs 4 5G cells — more balanced than USID_41 but still 4G-leaning; partial 5G availability for capable devices via 3500 MHz.
Capacity score 22.4 is adequate; tall_macro profile makes it a coverage anchor rather than a high-density capacity node.

nsa_5g_downgrade_risk.explanation: Primary backup USID_27 has 8 5G cells — exceeding USID_00's 6 — so no NSA downgrade on the primary handover path. USID_29 and USID_37 also carry 6 5G cells each. Only USID_41 (2 5G cells, 34.6% of target area) and USID_31 (4 5G cells, 7.7%) present partial 5G step-down risk; neither meets the NSA flag trigger condition (primary backup with 0 5G cells).

capacity_verdict_reasoning: Primary backup USID_27 (23.4) and secondary backups USID_29 and USID_37 (both 25.6) have capacity scores at or above USID_00 (25.6), covering the majority of displaced traffic with equivalent or better capacity.
All post_outage_load_factors ≤ 0.013 (Stage 1) — existing spare capacity at all backup sites is more than sufficient; no site approaches any load risk threshold.
USID_41's below-average score (15.6) and 4G-dominant profile is a localized concern for ~34.6% of USID_00's area, but its signal quality is strong and load increase is negligible.
key_findings_for_stage4: No NSA 5G downgrade on the primary handover path — USID_27 carries 8 5G cells, more than USID_00.
USID_41 presents a localized 5G service step-down for ~34.6% of USID_00's area: 4G-dominant (8×4G, 2×5G), no 3500 MHz, capacity score 15.6 vs 25.6.
Three of five backup sites (USID_27, USID_29, USID_37) match or exceed USID_00's capacity profile — the neighborhood is well-equipped for this outage.
